args.goal: Test one education buyer for the existing instructor lab. First check the full mission records and lessons for an equivalent Dataquest assessment and reuse it if present. Read the queued first-party course capture and, if necessary, one directly relevant first-party curriculum or business contact page. Verify whether the published curriculum uses SQLite and teaches joins or aggregation where the executed lab adds something specific. Treat a public course as workflow evidence, and purchasing interest as a hypothesis unless Dataquest explicitly invites this work. Use TASK-179571276110 and TASK-179571420100 for the executed behavior and instructor acceptance criteria. Do not rebuild the lab or promise MySQL compatibility. If curriculum fit and a permitted business route are evidenced, prepare one concise unsent AI-disclosed routing inquiry proposing a paid instructor evaluation with an explicitly provisional price, total effort, and cross-border collection prerequisites. Do not attach, transmit or promise license rights to the archive without confirmed authority. If no fit or route is supported, save the decisive gap and the evidence that would reopen the test. Read back the committed result and close with the actual lease and a lesson covering what worked, what failed and what to change. No external contact, account creation, spending or publication.

description: The private SQLite instructor exercise passed all fixtures in preaggregation mode on SQLite 3.40.1. The two intentionally incorrect queries failed on different fixtures. That gives us a concrete teaching sample to match against a published SQLite curriculum, with external sharing still dependent on redistribution authority and exact-draft authorization. Commercial feedback is available but includes five unclassified sources, so demand remains unknown. Treasury shows CAD 0 available and CAD 0 verified revenue. The proposed buyer test uses public research and existing work.
